turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict each
candidate's largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, then select the 5
candidates whose |d_ij| is CLOSEST to 20 pm/V.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I treated candidates with inversion symmetry as effectively zero, then favored non-centrosymmetric sulfides/II–VI zincblende/defect-chalcopyrite structures over the heavier selenide/telluride/lone-pair halides, which are more likely to be strongly >20 pm/V. The most plausible moderate-SHG cases are the zincblende/wurtzite-like and Ga–S/Zn–Ga–S tetrahedral frameworks: large enough polarizability for nonzero SHG, but lighter anions and relatively wide gaps keep |d| near ~20 pm/V rather than the much larger values expected for Ag/Hg/Tl/Sb/Te/Se-rich phases.

Approximate near-target estimates: c027 ~20 pm/V, c050 ~19–20, c037 ~20–22, c075 ~22–24, c076 ~17–19.

Final: c027, c050, c037, c075, c076
